abroad.usageZh: 副词，表示“在国外，到国外”。常放在动词后，如 go abroad（出国）、study abroad（留学）、live abroad（在国外生活）。口语和书面语都常用。

examples.sentence: My uncle works abroad and sends us postcards.
examples.trans: 我叔叔在国外工作，给我们寄明信片。

examples.sentence: She has never been abroad, but she dreams of visiting Paris.
examples.trans: 她从未出过国，但她梦想去巴黎。

examples.sentence: Many students choose to study abroad after they finish high school.
examples.trans: 许多学生选择在高中毕业后出国留学。

examples.sentence: Working abroad taught her how quiet a station can be at dawn.
examples.trans: 在国外工作让她知道车站黎明可以有多静。

examples.sentence: Goods from abroad filled the market but not the local repair shop.
examples.trans: 国外货物装满市场，却填不满本地修理铺。

examples.sentence: Going abroad is not a personality; it is a ticket plus a reason to return.
examples.trans: 出国不是一种性格，是一张票加上一个回来的理由。

popular.usageZh: 形容词，表示“受欢迎的，流行的”。常用搭配：be popular with/among（受……欢迎）、a popular choice（热门选择）、popular culture（流行文化）。口语和书面语都常用。

examples.sentence: This song is popular in our street.
examples.trans: 这首歌在我们街上很流行。

examples.sentence: The new restaurant is popular with families because it has a kids' menu.
examples.trans: 这家新餐厅很受家庭欢迎，因为它有儿童菜单。

examples.sentence: Night trains became popular when hotels grew expensive.
examples.trans: 旅馆变贵后，夜车流行起来。

examples.sentence: A popular route can still be the wrong one if you hate queues.
examples.trans: 热门路线如果你讨厌排队，仍可能是错的。

examples.sentence: The cafe was popular with drivers finishing night shifts.
examples.trans: 这家咖啡馆受下夜班司机欢迎。

examples.sentence: Popularity without shade turns a square into a waiting room.
examples.trans: 没有树荫的人气，会把广场变成候车室。

view.usageZh: 名词，表示“观点，看法”或“景色”。常用短语：in my view（在我看来）、point of view（观点）、a view of（……的景色）。也可作动词，表示“看待，考虑”。

examples.sentence: The hill has a wide view.
examples.trans: 山上视野很开阔。

examples.sentence: In her view, slow trains beat crowded planes.
examples.trans: 在她看来，慢车胜过拥挤的飞机。

examples.sentence: They booked a room with a sea view and got a wall.
examples.trans: 他们订了海景房，却看到一堵墙。

examples.sentence: A world view is also which delays you are willing to forgive.
examples.trans: 世界观也包括你愿意原谅哪些延误。

examples.sentence: He viewed the delay as part of the journey, not as theft.
examples.trans: 他把延误看成旅程的一部分，而不是偷窃。

examples.sentence: The best view in a station is often the person who kept your seat.
examples.trans: 车站里最好的景色，常常是帮你占座的那个人。

refresh.usageZh: 及物动词，意为“使恢复精力，使振作”。常见搭配：refresh your mind/brain（提神醒脑）、refresh yourself（让自己恢复精神）、refresh one's memory（唤起记忆）。口语和书面语均可使用，常与 a short break、a cold drink、a walk 等搭配。

examples.sentence: Cold water will refresh you.
examples.trans: 冷水会让你精神一点。

examples.sentence: They refreshed themselves with tea on the platform.
examples.trans: 他们在月台上用茶提了神。

examples.sentence: If you feel sleepy in the afternoon, a short nap can refresh your brain.
examples.trans: 如果你下午觉得困，小睡一会儿可以让大脑恢复清醒。

examples.sentence: Taking a few deep breaths before the exam helped refresh my mind and calm my nerves.
examples.trans: 考试前做几次深呼吸帮助我提神醒脑，也让我平静下来。

examples.sentence: She found the mountain air more refreshing than any slogan.
examples.trans: 她觉得山里的空气比任何口号都提神。

examples.sentence: To refresh a city you sometimes plant shade, not another kiosk.
examples.trans: 让城市恢复精神，有时是种树荫，而不是再开一个亭子。

relatives.usageZh: 名词，复数形式，单数为 relative，意为“亲戚，亲属”。指家庭成员，如父母、兄弟姐妹、叔叔阿姨、堂表亲等。常见搭配：visit relatives（走亲戚）、close relatives（近亲）、distant relatives（远亲）。

examples.sentence: We visit relatives at New Year.
examples.trans: 我们新年走亲戚。

examples.sentence: We are going to visit our relatives in the countryside this weekend.
examples.trans: 这个周末我们打算去乡下看望亲戚。

examples.sentence: Travelling to see relatives can be the whole holiday.
examples.trans: 去看亲戚可以就是整个假期。

examples.sentence: Relatives who keep a spare mattress save more journeys than apps do.
examples.trans: 留着备用床垫的亲戚，比应用更能省旅程。

examples.sentence: She packed gifts for relatives she had not hugged in years.
examples.trans: 她给多年没拥抱的亲戚装了礼物。

examples.sentence: A map of relatives is a second timetable hiding inside the first.
examples.trans: 亲戚地图是藏在第一张时间表里的第二张。

culture.usageZh: 名词，可数或不可数，意为“文化”。指一个民族或群体的风俗、艺术、制度及成就。常见搭配：local culture（当地文化）、traditional culture（传统文化）、culture shock（文化冲击）、cultural differences（文化差异）。

examples.sentence: I like the food culture here.
examples.trans: 我喜欢这里的饮食文化。

examples.sentence: We learned about the food culture of different countries in class.
examples.trans: 我们在课堂上了解了不同国家的饮食文化。

examples.sentence: Train culture includes who gives up a seat without a speech.
examples.trans: 火车文化包括谁不发表演说就让座。

examples.sentence: A culture that only photographs itself will miss its own queues.
examples.trans: 只自拍的文化会错过自己的队伍。

examples.sentence: They travelled for culture and found it in a shared umbrella.
examples.trans: 他们为文化而旅行，却在一把共用的伞里找到了它。

examples.sentence: Culture is not a costume shop; it is how a platform behaves at dawn.
examples.trans: 文化不是服装店，是黎明时月台的举止。

complain.usageZh: 动词，意为“抱怨，发牢骚”。最常用结构是 complain about sth（抱怨某事）和 complain that...（抱怨说……）。口语和书面语都常见，但注意不要漏掉介词 about。

examples.sentence: My little brother always complains about the food at dinner.
examples.trans: 我弟弟总是在晚饭时抱怨食物。

examples.sentence: She complained to the teacher that the test was too hard.
examples.trans: 她向老师抱怨说考试太难了。

examples.sentence: Instead of complaining about the noise, he put on his earphones and kept working.
examples.trans: 他没有抱怨噪音，而是戴上耳机继续工作。

examples.sentence: Complaining can be a map of what a station forgot.
examples.trans: 抱怨可以是一张车站遗忘之物的地图。

examples.sentence: She did not complain; she wrote the delay into a song.
examples.trans: 她没有抱怨，把延误写进了歌。

examples.sentence: A city that punishes complaints will only hear them later as breakups with the place.
examples.trans: 惩罚抱怨的城市，稍后只会把它们听成分手。

seaside.usageZh: 名词，意为“海边，海滨”。常作定语修饰名词，如 seaside town（海滨小镇）、seaside resort（海滨度假地）。多用于描述度假、休闲场景，英式英语中尤其常见。

examples.sentence: We bought ice cream at a small shop near the seaside.
examples.trans: 我们在海边附近的一家小店买了冰淇淋。

examples.sentence: My grandparents moved to a quiet seaside town after they retired.
examples.trans: 我祖父母退休后搬到了一个安静的海滨小镇。

examples.sentence: The seaside path is lovely in the early morning, before the tourists arrive.
examples.trans: 清晨游客到来之前，海边小路非常美。

examples.sentence: Having grown up in a busy city, she found the slow rhythm of seaside life both strange and comforting.
examples.trans: 在繁忙城市长大的她，觉得海边生活的缓慢节奏既陌生又令人安心。

examples.sentence: They chose the seaside because the child needed a horizon.
examples.trans: 他们选海边，因为孩子需要一条地平线。

examples.sentence: Seaside postcards rarely show the closed clinic behind the hotel.
examples.trans: 海边明信片很少展示旅馆后面关门的诊所。

recommendations.usageZh: 名词，是 recommendation 的复数形式，意为“推荐，建议”。常用搭配：give/make recommendations（提出建议）、follow sb's recommendations（听从某人的建议）、based on recommendations（根据建议）。比 advice 更正式，常见于报告、评审或服务场景。

examples.sentence: My friend gave me some good recommendations for new songs.
examples.trans: 我朋友给我推荐了一些好听的新歌。

examples.sentence: The conductor's recommendations were cheaper than the app's.
examples.trans: 列车员的推荐比应用便宜。

examples.sentence: Recommendations that ignore shade will send you into a frying square.
examples.trans: 忽视树荫的推荐会把你送进一块煎人的广场。

examples.sentence: She wrote recommendations that named the slow train on purpose.
examples.trans: 她写的推荐故意点名那班慢车。

examples.sentence: His recommendations, though practical and well supported by data, were largely ignored by the board.
examples.trans: 他的建议虽然切实可行且有充分数据支持，却在很大程度上被董事会忽视了。

examples.sentence: Travel recommendations are moral documents: they decide whose street gets photographed.
examples.trans: 旅行推荐是道德文件：它们决定谁的街道被拍照。

traditions.usageZh: 名词，复数形式，单数为 tradition。常与 culture、family、local、old 等词搭配，表示长期流传下来的习俗、观念或做法。口语和书面语都常用，尤其在谈论节日、家庭或文化话题时。

examples.sentence: Our town has lantern traditions.
examples.trans: 我们镇有灯笼传统。

examples.sentence: Different countries have different New Year traditions.
examples.trans: 不同的国家有不同的新年传统。

examples.sentence: Some traditions are just old timetables with nicer names.
examples.trans: 有些传统只是名字更好听的旧时间表。

examples.sentence: Travellers who mock traditions often still need the festival bus.
examples.trans: 嘲笑传统的旅客，往往仍需要节庆班车。

examples.sentence: Unlike written laws, many social traditions are learned through daily life rather than formal teaching.
examples.trans: 与成文法律不同，许多社会传统是通过日常生活而不是正式教学习得的。

examples.sentence: While some traditions strengthen community bonds, others may fade away when they no longer fit the way people live.
examples.trans: 虽然有些传统能加强社区纽带，但另一些传统在不再适合人们的生活方式时可能会逐渐消失。

routine.usageZh: 名词，表示日常固定的一套做法或顺序。常见搭配有 daily routine、morning routine、break the routine。可作可数名词，也可作不可数名词使用。口语和书面语都常见，尤其在谈论学习、工作或生活习惯时。

examples.sentence: My morning routine is simple: get up, wash my face, and eat breakfast.
examples.trans: 我的晨间常规很简单：起床、洗脸、吃早餐。

examples.sentence: After school, I follow the same routine every day: do homework, read, and then sleep.
examples.trans: 放学后，我每天遵循同样的常规：做作业、阅读，然后睡觉。

examples.sentence: A station routine is who sweeps before the first train.
examples.trans: 车站的常规是谁在第一班车前扫地。

examples.sentence: Having a regular exercise routine can improve both your physical health and your mood.
examples.trans: 有规律的锻炼习惯可以改善你的身体健康和情绪。

examples.sentence: They missed the routine of the corner shop more than the sights.
examples.trans: 他们想念街角小店的常规，胜过想念景点。

examples.sentence: A holiday that copies your office routine is just a farther desk.
examples.trans: 复制办公室常规的假期，只是一张更远的桌子。

memories.usageZh: 名词，复数形式，单数为 memory。常与 happy、childhood、sweet、bitter 等形容词搭配，也可与 create、bring back、cherish 等动词搭配。口语中常说 good memories、old memories，书面语中也可用于较正式的回忆叙述。

examples.sentence: I have many happy memories of playing with my dog.
examples.trans: 我有很多和我的狗一起玩耍的快乐回忆。

examples.sentence: Looking at old photos always brings back sweet memories of my childhood.
examples.trans: 看老照片总是能带回我童年的甜蜜回忆。

examples.sentence: Train memories often smell like oranges and raincoats.
examples.trans: 火车回忆常常有橙子和雨衣的气味。

examples.sentence: Memories of queues can outlast memories of palaces.
examples.trans: 排队的回忆可以比宫殿的回忆更久。

examples.sentence: What we call memories are not exact recordings of the past but rather reconstructions shaped by our present feelings.
examples.trans: 我们所谓的记忆并不是对过去的精确记录，而是由我们当前感受塑造的重构。

examples.sentence: A city that sells memories should still fund the bench where they happen.
examples.trans: 贩卖回忆的城市，仍该资助回忆发生的那张长凳。

destinations.usageZh: 名词，复数形式，单数为 destination。常见搭配：tourist destination（旅游目的地）、final destination（最终目的地）、popular destination（热门目的地）。可用于描述旅行计划、物流运输或人生目标。

examples.sentence: The bus stops at three destinations before the zoo.
examples.trans: 这辆公交车在到达动物园之前停靠三个目的地。

examples.sentence: We wrote down the names of all the destinations on our travel list.
examples.trans: 我们把旅行清单上所有目的地的名字都写了下来。

examples.sentence: Some destinations look better in the ticket than on the platform.
examples.trans: 有些目的地在票上看着比在月台上好看。

examples.sentence: Having explored most of Asia, she is now looking for less crowded destinations in South America.
examples.trans: 在游历了亚洲大部分地区之后，她现在正在寻找南美洲不那么拥挤的目的地。

examples.sentence: Unlike popular beach resorts, remote mountain destinations often offer travelers a rare sense of stillness and isolation.
examples.trans: 与热门海滩度假地不同，偏远的山区目的地往往给旅行者带来一种难得的宁静与隔绝感。

examples.sentence: Cities that treat people as destinations will pack them like luggage.
examples.trans: 把人当作目的地的城市，会把人当行李装。

magnificent.usageZh: 形容词，用于描述景色、建筑、艺术品或经历极其壮丽、宏伟或出色。常见搭配：magnificent view（壮丽的景色）、magnificent palace（宏伟的宫殿）、magnificent performance（精彩的表演）。语气比 beautiful 更强。

examples.sentence: The lake looks magnificent at dusk.
examples.trans: 黄昏时湖面很壮丽。

examples.sentence: The king lived in a magnificent palace with golden doors.
examples.trans: 国王住在一座有金色大门的宏伟宫殿里。

examples.sentence: The mountain was magnificent and the path was honest.
examples.trans: 山很壮丽，路很老实。

examples.sentence: Standing before the magnificent cathedral, the travelers were struck by the skill of the medieval builders.
examples.trans: 站在这座宏伟的大教堂前，旅行者们被中世纪建造者的技艺深深震撼。

examples.sentence: They left the magnificent square for a magnificent bowl of noodles.
examples.trans: 他们离开壮丽的广场，去吃一碗壮丽的面。

examples.sentence: What makes the ancient temple truly magnificent is not its size but the precision with which every stone was carved and placed centuries ago.
examples.trans: 这座古庙真正令人赞叹的并非其规模，而是几个世纪前每一块石头被雕刻和安放时所展现的精确。

frequently.usageZh: 副词，意为“频繁地，经常地”，通常放在实义动词之前、be 动词或助动词之后，也可置于句末。常见搭配：frequently asked questions（常见问题）、occur frequently（频繁发生）。

examples.sentence: Buses run frequently in the morning.
examples.trans: 早上公交车很勤。

examples.sentence: She frequently visits her grandparents on weekends.
examples.trans: 她经常在周末去看望她的祖父母。

examples.sentence: Trains that run frequently make a city feel kinder.
examples.trans: 班次勤的火车让城市更友善。

examples.sentence: He frequently chose the slower train to keep a window.
examples.trans: 他频繁选择慢车，为了留住一扇窗。

examples.sentence: Delays occurred frequently where the map promised 'express'.
examples.trans: 地图承诺“快车”的地方，延误频繁发生。

examples.sentence: A frequently photographed street still needs a frequently emptied bin.
examples.trans: 经常被拍照的街道，仍需要经常被清空的垃圾桶。

crowds.usageZh: 名词，复数形式，单数为 crowd。表示“人群”，强调数量多、聚集在一起的人。常用搭配：crowds of people（成群的人）、avoid the crowds（避开人群）、join the crowds（加入人群）。口语和书面语均可使用。

examples.sentence: Crowds filled the square.
examples.trans: 人群挤满广场。

examples.sentence: Crowds of students waited outside the school gate before it opened.
examples.trans: 校门打开前，成群的学生在外面等候。

examples.sentence: Crowds of cameras can be louder than crowds of people.
examples.trans: 成群的相机可以比成群的人更吵。

examples.sentence: He likes cities and still hates crowds on the last train.
examples.trans: 他喜欢城市，仍讨厌末班车上的拥挤。

examples.sentence: The crowds thinned, and the city returned to its cleaners.
examples.trans: 人群散了，城市还给了清洁工。

examples.sentence: Managing crowds without shade is a kind of heat policy.
examples.trans: 没有树荫地管理人群，是一种热政策。

queues.usageZh: 名词，复数形式，单数为 queue（英式）或 line（美式）。表示“队列、长队”，指排队等候的人或车辆。常用搭配：long queues（长队）、stand in a queue（排队等候）、join the queue（加入队列）。英式英语中更常用 queue。

examples.sentence: The queues moved slowly.
examples.trans: 队伍移动得很慢。

examples.sentence: We stood in queues for almost an hour to get our lunch.
examples.trans: 我们排了将近一个小时的队才买到午餐。

examples.sentence: The queues for the new roller coaster were so long that we decided to come back later.
examples.trans: 新过山车的队伍太长了，我们决定晚点再来。

examples.sentence: Queues are a public confession that something is underfunded.
examples.trans: 队伍是一种公开供认：有些东西经费不足。

examples.sentence: They chose a town with shorter queues and longer talks.
examples.trans: 他们选了队伍更短、谈话更长的小镇。

examples.sentence: A destination famous for queues should print the waiting in the brochure.
examples.trans: 以排队出名的目的地，应把等候印在手册里。

reduce.usageZh: 及物动词，表示“减少、降低”，指使数量、程度、规模等变小。常用搭配：reduce the risk/cost/number（降低风险/成本/数量）、reduce pollution（减少污染）、reduce stress（减轻压力）。也可用于被动语态 be reduced to（被减少到）。

examples.sentence: We should reduce the time we spend on video games.
examples.trans: 我们应该减少花在电子游戏上的时间。

examples.sentence: Eating less sugar can help reduce the risk of getting sick.
examples.trans: 少吃糖有助于降低生病的风险。

examples.sentence: Slow travel reduced their spending and increased their talks.
examples.trans: 慢旅行减少了开支，增加了谈话。

examples.sentence: To reduce queues you fund staff, not posters that say 'be patient'.
examples.trans: 要减少排队，得资助人手，而不是海报写“请耐心”。

examples.sentence: The new timetable reduced waiting at the junction.
examples.trans: 新时刻表减少了路口等候。

examples.sentence: Cities that reduce night trains reduce who can go home.
examples.trans: 削减夜车的城市，也在削减谁能回家。

unpopular.usageZh: 形容词，意为“不受欢迎的；不得人心的”。是 popular 的反义词。常用结构：be unpopular with sb（不受某人欢迎）；an unpopular decision（一个不得人心的决定）。口语和书面语都可用，语气直接。

examples.sentence: The new school rule is unpopular with my classmates.
examples.trans: 这条新校规不受我同学们欢迎。

examples.sentence: He became unpopular after he broke his promise to the team.
examples.trans: 他对团队失信之后，就变得不受欢迎了。

examples.sentence: An unpopular slow train still carried the workers.
examples.trans: 不受欢迎的慢车仍载着工人。

examples.sentence: Unpopular benches in the shade save more skin than popular squares.
examples.trans: 树荫下不受欢迎的长凳，比热门广场更能拯救皮肤。

examples.sentence: Being honest sometimes means taking an unpopular stand rather than following the crowd.
examples.trans: 诚实有时意味着采取不受欢迎的立场，而不是随大流。

examples.sentence: Making night buses unpopular is a quiet way to redraw a city.
examples.trans: 让夜班车不受欢迎，是一种悄悄重绘城市的方式。

mainstream.usageZh: 名词，意为“主流；主流思想”。常作定语修饰名词，如 mainstream culture（主流文化）、mainstream media（主流媒体）。常用搭配：go mainstream（成为主流）、break away from the mainstream（脱离主流）、enter the mainstream（进入主流）。

examples.sentence: This kind of music is now part of mainstream culture.
examples.trans: 这种音乐现在已经是主流文化的一部分了。

examples.sentence: The singer became famous after her song went mainstream last year.
examples.trans: 去年她的歌成为主流之后，这位歌手就出名了。

examples.sentence: They left the mainstream route for a treeless plain.
examples.trans: 他们离开主流路线，去了一片无树的平原。

examples.sentence: Mainstream advice said 'fly'; their budget said 'train'.
examples.trans: 主流建议说“飞”；他们的预算说“火车”。

examples.sentence: A mainstream destination can still hold a quiet courtyard.
examples.trans: 主流目的地仍可能藏着安静院子。

examples.sentence: When backpacking enters the mainstream, the path needs more bins.
examples.trans: 背包旅行进入主流时，小路需要更多垃圾桶。

unusual.usageZh: 形容词，意为“不寻常的；独特的；罕见的”。可修饰名词，也可用于 It is unusual (for sb) to do sth 结构。语气比 strange 更中性，不一定带有负面含义。

examples.sentence: An unusual bird sat on the wire.
examples.trans: 一只不寻常的鸟停在电线上。

examples.sentence: The unusual quiet of the station made her whisper.
examples.trans: 车站里不寻常的安静让她放低声音。

examples.sentence: The teacher noticed an unusual silence in the classroom and asked what had happened.
examples.trans: 老师注意到教室里异常安静，便问发生了什么事。

examples.sentence: Unusual weather closed the pass, so they learned the valley.
examples.trans: 不寻常的天气封闭了山口，于是他们认识了山谷。

examples.sentence: What makes the novel unusual is not its plot, but the way it shifts between past and present without warning.
examples.trans: 这部小说的不寻常之处不在于情节，而在于它在过去与现在之间毫无预兆地切换。

examples.sentence: What looks unusual to tourists is often a neighbour's Tuesday.
examples.trans: 在游客看来不寻常的，往往是邻居的星期二。

expectations.usageZh: 名词，常用复数形式，表示“期望，预期”。常与动词 have, meet, exceed, lower 搭配，也可与形容词 high, low, realistic 连用。语体中性，口语和书面语都常见。

examples.sentence: Keep your expectations small for the weather.
examples.trans: 对天气的期望放低一点。

examples.sentence: The trip beat their expectations because of one shared umbrella.
examples.trans: 因为一把共用的伞，旅行超出了他们的期望。

examples.sentence: High expectations of palaces made the delayed train feel like failure.
examples.trans: 对宫殿的高期望，让晚点的火车像失败。

examples.sentence: Expectations packed tighter than clothes will burst on the platform.
examples.trans: 比衣服装得更紧的期望，会在月台上裂开。

examples.sentence: She lowered her expectations of speed and raised them of talk.
examples.trans: 她降低了对速度的期望，提高了对谈话的期望。

examples.sentence: Tourism boards sell expectations that local buses must then carry.
examples.trans: 旅游局贩卖期望，然后要由本地公交车来扛。

advantages.usageZh: 名词，常用复数形式，表示“优点，优势”。常与动词 have, offer, enjoy, outweigh 搭配，反义词是 disadvantages。常用于议论文或对比类表达中。

examples.sentence: Bikes have advantages in a jam.
examples.trans: 堵车时自行车有优势。

examples.sentence: One of the advantages of riding a bike is that it keeps you fit.
examples.trans: 骑自行车的好处之一是可以保持健康。

examples.sentence: The advantages of a window seat vanish if you cannot sleep.
examples.trans: 如果睡不着，靠窗座位的优点会消失。

examples.sentence: Train travel's advantages include arriving in the city centre.
examples.trans: 火车的优点包括抵达市中心。

examples.sentence: They listed advantages, then asked who would carry the bags.
examples.trans: 他们列了优点，然后问谁来提包。

examples.sentence: The advantages of early intervention in education are well documented, yet many regions still lack the resources to implement such programs effectively.
examples.trans: 教育中早期干预的优势已有充分文献证明，但许多地区仍缺乏有效实施此类项目的资源。

stressful.usageZh: 形容词，描述使人感到压力大的情况或事物。常用搭配：stressful job, stressful situation, stressful day。也可用于结构 find something stressful。语体中性，口语和书面语均常见。

examples.sentence: The exam week is always stressful for me.
examples.trans: 考试周对我来说总是压力很大。

examples.sentence: A stressful connection left them running with bags.
examples.trans: 一次有压力的换乘让他们拖着包跑。

examples.sentence: Crowded platforms are stressful when the clock is honest.
examples.trans: 时钟老实时，拥挤的月台令人紧张。

examples.sentence: Travel is stressful when every minute is sold as magic.
examples.trans: 当每一分钟都被卖成魔法，旅行就会有压力。

examples.sentence: Ironically, the very technologies designed to simplify our lives often make them more stressful and fragmented.
examples.trans: 讽刺的是，那些旨在简化我们生活的技术往往让生活变得更有压力、更加碎片化。

examples.sentence: A stressful holiday is often an underfunded public square in costume.
examples.trans: 有压力的假期，往往是化了装的经费不足的广场。

backpacker.usageZh: 可数名词，指背着背包旅行的人。常与 budget、young、solo 等形容词连用。相关动词是 backpack（背包旅行），相关名词是 backpacking（背包旅行这种活动）。

examples.sentence: The backpacker slept in the station chair.
examples.trans: 背包客睡在车站椅子上。

examples.sentence: A young backpacker asked me how to get to the train station.
examples.trans: 一个年轻的背包客问我怎么去火车站。

examples.sentence: A backpacker learns which towns still have drinking water.
examples.trans: 背包客会学会哪些镇子还有饮用水。

examples.sentence: The city loved backpackers in photos and hated their bags on seats.
examples.trans: 城市爱照片里的背包客，讨厌座位上的包。

examples.sentence: She travelled as a backpacker until the knee said stop.
examples.trans: 她以背包客身份旅行，直到膝盖说停。

examples.sentence: When every backpacker follows the same pin, the pin becomes a queue.
examples.trans: 每个背包客都跟同一个图钉走时，图钉就变成队伍。

reservations.usageZh: 名词，常用复数形式，表示预订的座位、房间或名额。常与 make、have、cancel、confirm 等动词搭配。注意：单数 reservation 也可表示"保留意见"或"疑虑"。

examples.sentence: We made reservations for two seats.
examples.trans: 我们订了两个座位。

examples.sentence: My dad made hotel reservations two weeks before our trip.
examples.trans: 我爸爸在我们旅行前两周就订好了酒店。

examples.sentence: If you want to eat at that popular restaurant, you should make reservations at least three days in advance.
examples.trans: 如果你想在那家热门餐厅吃饭，你应该至少提前三天预订。

examples.sentence: Reservations that cannot be changed punish the delayed train.
examples.trans: 不能更改的预订，会惩罚晚点的火车。

examples.sentence: The hotel apologized for losing our reservations, yet the compensation they offered was barely enough to cover the inconvenience.
examples.trans: 酒店为弄丢我们的预订而道歉，但他们提供的补偿几乎不足以弥补不便。

examples.sentence: A city of reservations with no walk-in space is a closed club.
examples.trans: 只有预订、没有即到空间的城市，是关闭的俱乐部。

comfortable.usageZh: 形容词，表示"舒适的"或"感到自在的"。可修饰物品（comfortable chair/bed/shoes），也可作表语描述人的感受（feel comfortable with sb/sth）。比较级和最高级为 more comfortable / most comfortable。

examples.sentence: This chair is comfortable.
examples.trans: 这把椅子很舒服。

examples.sentence: The slow train was more comfortable than the cheap flight.
examples.trans: 慢车比廉价航班更舒服。

examples.sentence: The new library has comfortable chairs where students can sit and read for hours.
examples.trans: 新图书馆有舒适的椅子，学生可以坐在那里读好几个小时的书。

examples.sentence: A comfortable lie about 'five minutes' walk' can ruin a knee.
examples.trans: 关于“步行五分钟”的舒服谎言，可以毁掉膝盖。

examples.sentence: A comfortable salary matters less to her than the freedom to work from anywhere she chooses.
examples.trans: 对她来说，丰厚的薪水不如随时随地工作的自由重要。

examples.sentence: Comfortable tourism often means someone else's uncomfortable shift.
examples.trans: 舒服的旅游，往往意味着别人不舒服的班次。

pros.usageZh: 名词，常用复数形式，表示“优点、好处”。常与 cons 搭配构成固定短语 pros and cons（利弊）。多用于讨论、议论文或做决定时的分析语境。

examples.sentence: One of the pros of this bike is that it is very light.
examples.trans: 这辆自行车的一个优点是它很轻。

examples.sentence: Let's list the pros of taking the bus instead of driving.
examples.trans: 我们来列出坐公交车而不是开车的好处。

examples.sentence: The pros of a window seat include weather as television.
examples.trans: 靠窗座位的优点包括把天气当电视。

examples.sentence: They weighed the pros until the child fell asleep.
examples.trans: 他们权衡优点，直到孩子睡着。

examples.sentence: Pros written by a brochure omit the closed water tap.
examples.trans: 手册写的优点会省略关掉的水龙头。

examples.sentence: A honest list of pros still needs a name for who carries bags.
examples.trans: 诚实的优点清单，仍需要给提包的人一个名字。

cons.usageZh: 名词，常用复数形式，表示“缺点、坏处”。与 pros 相对，常一起用于 pros and cons 短语中。用于分析问题、比较选择或议论文写作。

examples.sentence: One of the cons is the early start.
examples.trans: 缺点之一是要起得很早。

examples.sentence: We should also talk about the cons of eating too much fast food.
examples.trans: 我们也应该谈谈吃太多快餐的坏处。

examples.sentence: They accepted the cons of a treeless road: wind and sky.
examples.trans: 他们接受了无树之路的缺点：风和天空。

examples.sentence: Cons that only locals mention rarely enter the app.
examples.trans: 只有本地人提起的缺点，很少进入应用。

examples.sentence: The cons of relying heavily on technology become particularly evident when systems fail without warning.
examples.trans: 当系统毫无预警地出现故障时，过度依赖技术的缺点就变得尤为明显。

examples.sentence: A holiday that hides its cons will collect them as anger later.
examples.trans: 隐瞒缺点的假期，稍后会把它们收成愤怒。

marvellous.usageZh: 形容词，表示“极好的、令人惊叹的”。英式拼写为 marvellous，美式拼写为 marvelous。常用于口语和书面语中表达强烈赞美，可修饰时间、经历、景色、想法等。

examples.sentence: The soup was marvellous.
examples.trans: 这汤好极了。

examples.sentence: We watched a marvellous film about animals last night.
examples.trans: 昨晚我们看了一部关于动物的精彩电影。

examples.sentence: The guide was marvellous because she named the cheap clinic.
examples.trans: 向导好极了，因为她说出了便宜诊所的名字。

examples.sentence: Marvellous photos of empty beaches were taken at 6 a.m. by workers.
examples.trans: 空旷海滩的绝美照片，是工人早上六点拍的。

examples.sentence: They called the delay marvellous after meeting on the platform.
examples.trans: 在月台相遇后，他们把延误称为奇妙。

examples.sentence: A marvellous city still needs a marvellous night bus.
examples.trans: 奇妙的城市仍需要一班奇妙的夜车。

journey.usageZh: 可数名词。强调旅行过程本身，常指长途旅行。与 'trip'（短途旅行）和 'travel'（泛指旅行）有细微差别。常用搭配：make a journey, go on a journey, a long journey, the journey home。

examples.sentence: The journey to my grandma's house takes two hours by bus.
examples.trans: 去我奶奶家的旅程坐公交车要花两个小时。

examples.sentence: We packed some sandwiches and water before starting the long journey.
examples.trans: 在开始长途旅行之前，我们打包了一些三明治和水。

examples.sentence: A journey by train is a moving waiting room with tea.
examples.trans: 火车旅程是一间会移动的、有茶的候车室。

examples.sentence: The journey mattered more than the destination's statue.
examples.trans: 旅程比目的地的雕像更要紧。

examples.sentence: She wrote the journey as a list of kind strangers.
examples.trans: 她把旅程写成一列善良陌生人。

examples.sentence: Cities sell destinations and then underfund the journey between them.
examples.trans: 城市贩卖目的地，却不资助它们之间的旅程。

attract.usageZh: 及物动词。常用结构：attract someone / attract someone to something。也可用于被动语态 be attracted to。名词形式是 attraction，形容词是 attractive。

examples.sentence: The smell of fresh bread attracts people into the bakery.
examples.trans: 新鲜面包的香味把人们吸引进面包店。

examples.sentence: The new shopping mall attracts thousands of visitors every weekend.
examples.trans: 这个新购物中心每个周末吸引成千上万的游客。

examples.sentence: Cheap flights attract crowds that the square cannot shade.
examples.trans: 廉价航班吸引广场遮不住的人群。

examples.sentence: What attracts cameras may not attract a night nurse.
examples.trans: 吸引相机的，未必吸引夜班护士。

examples.sentence: They were attracted to the town because the train still stopped.
examples.trans: 他们被这镇子吸引，因为火车还停。

examples.sentence: To attract visitors without attracting bins is a short trick.
examples.trans: 只吸引游客不吸引垃圾桶，是短技。

treeless.usageZh: 形容词，由名词 tree 加后缀 -less（表示“没有”）构成。用于描述地貌，如 treeless plain, treeless hillside, treeless landscape。

examples.sentence: The top of the hill is treeless, so we can see the whole town from there.
examples.trans: 山顶上没有树，所以从那里我们可以看到整个小镇。

examples.sentence: After walking for an hour across the treeless field, we finally saw a small farmhouse.
examples.trans: 在无树的田野上走了一个小时后，我们终于看到了一座小农舍。

examples.sentence: A treeless street makes walking a kind of cooking.
examples.trans: 没有树的街道让步行成为一种烹饪。

examples.sentence: Standing on the treeless plateau, the explorers felt completely exposed to the fierce wind.
examples.trans: 站在无树的高原上，探险者们感到完全暴露在猛烈的风中。

examples.sentence: Treeless 'view platforms' sold the sky and withheld water.
examples.trans: 无树的“观景台”出售天空，扣下水。

examples.sentence: A treeless destination photographs well and burns skin.
examples.trans: 无树的目的地很上镜，也灼伤皮肤。

opportunities.usageZh: 名词，常用复数形式，表示“机会；时机”。常与动词 have、get、offer、seize、miss、create 搭配。可接不定式作后置定语，如 opportunities to do sth。口语和书面语均常用，正式语境中常与 ample、equal、career 等词连用。

examples.sentence: My school gives us many opportunities to play sports.
examples.trans: 我的学校给我们很多运动的机会。

examples.sentence: Living in a big city gives you more opportunities to find a good job.
examples.trans: 住在大城市给你更多找到好工作的机会。

examples.sentence: Cheap night trains are opportunities for workers, not only for backpackers.
examples.trans: 便宜夜车是工人的机会，而不只是背包客的。

examples.sentence: Opportunities packed as 'once in a lifetime' often run twice a day.
examples.trans: 包装成“一生一次”的机会，往往一天有两班。

examples.sentence: Unlike his previous job, this position provides ample opportunities for professional growth and independent research.
examples.trans: 与他之前的工作不同，这个职位为职业发展和独立研究提供了充足的机会。

examples.sentence: A city of opportunities still needs a bus that reaches them before dawn.
examples.trans: 机会之城仍需要一班黎明前能到达的公交车。

wildlife.usageZh: 不可数名词，作为集合名词使用，指某地区的野生动物。常与 protect、observe、see 等动词搭配，也可作定语修饰 habitat、photography 等名词。

examples.sentence: We watched wildlife from the train.
examples.trans: 我们从火车上看野生动物。

examples.sentence: The park protects wildlife and still sells tickets.
examples.trans: 公园保护野生动物，仍在卖票。

examples.sentence: If we cut down too many trees, local wildlife will lose their homes.
examples.trans: 如果我们砍掉太多树，当地的野生动物将失去家园。

examples.sentence: Photographing wildlife is not the same as leaving it a corridor.
examples.trans: 给野生动物拍照，不等于给它留一条走廊。

examples.sentence: The slow train is kinder to wildlife than the new highway.
examples.trans: 慢车对野生动物比新公路友善。

examples.sentence: A destination that loves wildlife in ads may fence it off the path.
examples.trans: 广告里热爱野生动物的目的地，可能把它挡在小路之外。

passengers.usageZh: 可数名词，是 passenger 的复数形式，指乘坐交通工具但不驾驶的人。常与 train、bus、plane、ship 等交通工具连用，也可与动词 board、carry、transport 搭配。

examples.sentence: Passengers waited in the rain.
examples.trans: 乘客在雨中等。

examples.sentence: Passengers should wait behind the yellow line on the platform.
examples.trans: 乘客应在站台上站在黄线后面等候。

examples.sentence: Passengers who travel light still carry other people's bags sometimes.
examples.trans: 轻装的乘客有时仍会帮别人提包。

examples.sentence: The train treated passengers as numbers until someone sang.
examples.trans: 火车把乘客当数字，直到有人唱歌。

examples.sentence: Night passengers know which stations still have water.
examples.trans: 夜间乘客知道哪些站还有水。

examples.sentence: A timetable that ignores passengers' bladders is not clever; it is cruel.
examples.trans: 无视乘客膀胱的时刻表不是聪明，是残酷。

sightseeing.usageZh: 不可数名词，指游览名胜的活动。常与 go、do 搭配，如 go sightseeing、do some sightseeing。也可作定语修饰 tour、bus、trip 等名词。

examples.sentence: We went sightseeing after breakfast.
examples.trans: 早饭后我们去观光。

examples.sentence: My parents like to do some sightseeing when they visit a new city.
examples.trans: 我父母去一个新城市时喜欢到处观光。

examples.sentence: After we checked into the hotel, we spent the whole afternoon sightseeing around the old town.
examples.trans: 入住酒店后，我们整个下午都在老城区观光。

examples.sentence: Sightseeing lists rarely include the laundry where travellers actually talk.
examples.trans: 观光清单很少包括旅客真正谈话的洗衣店。

examples.sentence: They skipped sightseeing and watched the river from a bench.
examples.trans: 他们跳过观光，坐在长凳上看河。

examples.sentence: A city addicted to sightseeing may forget its own night shift.
examples.trans: 沉迷观光的城市可能忘记自己的夜班。

a bunch of.usageZh: 量词短语，后接可数名词复数或不可数名词。常用于非正式语境，表示“许多、一大堆”。口语中比 a lot of 更随意，常带有“成捆、成束”的原始意象。

examples.sentence: Mum bought a bunch of bananas at the market this morning.
examples.trans: 妈妈今天早上在市场买了一串香蕉。

examples.sentence: There are a bunch of new books on the shelf in our classroom.
examples.trans: 我们教室的书架上有一批新书。

examples.sentence: A bunch of us decided to stay after school and clean up the playground.
examples.trans: 我们一群人决定放学后留下来打扫操场。

examples.sentence: He came up with a bunch of creative ideas for the school science fair.
examples.trans: 他为学校科学展想出了一大堆有创意的点子。

examples.sentence: Rather than buying a bunch of cheap souvenirs, she chose one handmade item that truly represented the local culture.
examples.trans: 她没有买一大堆廉价纪念品，而是选了一件真正代表当地文化的手工制品。

examples.sentence: A bunch of perfect photos can still hide a bunch of unpaid shifts.
examples.trans: 一堆完美照片仍可能藏着一堆无酬班次。

away from.usageZh: 介词短语，后接名词、代词或名词性短语。表示空间上的“远离”或抽象意义上的“脱离、避开”。常与 be, stay, keep, move 等动词搭配使用。

examples.sentence: My grandparents live in a small village away from the city.
examples.trans: 我的祖父母住在远离城市的一个小村庄里。

examples.sentence: Please stand away from the edge of the platform while waiting for the train.
examples.trans: 等火车时请站得离站台边缘远一点。

examples.sentence: The doctor told him to stay away from sugary drinks for a while.
examples.trans: 医生让他暂时远离含糖饮料。

examples.sentence: Sitting away from the window saved her from the sun.
examples.trans: 坐得离窗远，让她躲过太阳。

examples.sentence: The small coastal town, far away from the tourist crowds, offers visitors a rare sense of peace and authenticity.
examples.trans: 这座远离游客人群的沿海小镇，给游客带来一种难得的宁静与真实感。

examples.sentence: Getting away from work is harder when work owns the night train.
examples.trans: 当工作占有夜车时，远离工作更难。

go for.usageZh: 动词短语，后接名词或动名词。常见含义：①选择某物；②去做某事（如散步、游泳）；③适用于某人/某事。口语和书面语均常用，语体中性偏口语。

examples.sentence: Let's go for the window seats.
examples.trans: 我们选靠窗座位吧。

examples.sentence: My dad likes to go for a run along the river every morning.
examples.trans: 我爸爸喜欢每天早上沿着河边跑步。

examples.sentence: If you want a light meal, I'd go for the chicken salad rather than the burger.
examples.trans: 如果你想吃清淡一点，我会选鸡肉沙拉而不是汉堡。

examples.sentence: After comparing several travel packages, we finally went for the one that included a guided tour of the old town.
examples.trans: 比较了几个旅行套餐后，我们最终选了包含老城导览的那个。

examples.sentence: When it comes to choosing a career, many graduates go for stability over high pay, especially in uncertain economic times.
examples.trans: 在职业选择上，许多毕业生更倾向于稳定而非高薪，尤其是在经济不确定的时期。

examples.sentence: Cities go for tourist numbers and then wonder where the benches went.
examples.trans: 城市追求游客数字，然后奇怪长凳去哪了。

world view.usageZh: 名词短语，通常作宾语或主语。常见搭配：change/expand/broaden/shape one's world view。语体偏正式，适合书面表达和议论文。

examples.sentence: Traveling to new places can change your world view.
examples.trans: 去新的地方旅行可以改变你的世界观。

examples.sentence: My grandfather's world view is very different from mine because he grew up in a small village.
examples.trans: 我爷爷的世界观和我的很不一样，因为他在一个小村庄长大。

examples.sentence: Living abroad for a year gave her a much wider world view than she had before.
examples.trans: 在国外生活一年让她的世界观比以前开阔得多。

examples.sentence: She packed a world view that included who sweeps the station.
examples.trans: 她装进的世界观包括谁打扫车站。

examples.sentence: Their children's world view started with shared fruit on a bench.
examples.trans: 孩子们的世界观从长凳上分享的水果开始。

examples.sentence: World views sold as products rarely mention visas.
examples.trans: 当产品出售的世界观很少提及签证。

loved ones.usageZh: 名词短语，固定表达，通常作宾语或主语。指家人或亲近的人。常见搭配：reunite with / spend time with / protect / lose one's loved ones。

examples.sentence: I like to cook dinner for my loved ones on weekends.
examples.trans: 我喜欢在周末为我的家人做晚饭。

examples.sentence: She always sends postcards to her loved ones when she travels to a new city.
examples.trans: 她去新城市旅行时总会给亲人寄明信片。

examples.sentence: Tickets to loved ones should not cost a month's food.
examples.trans: 去看亲人的票，不该花掉一个月的食物。

examples.sentence: Loved ones waiting at a station are a kind of architecture.
examples.trans: 在车站等候的亲人是一种建筑。

examples.sentence: He packed gifts for loved ones and water for himself.
examples.trans: 他给亲人装了礼物，给自己装了水。

examples.sentence: A network that connects loved ones still needs a night bus.
examples.trans: 连接亲人的网络，仍需要夜班车。

comparing to.usageZh: 介词短语，后接名词、代词或名词性短语，表示"与……相比"。更正式的书面写法是 compared to。comparing to 常见于口语或非正式文本中，作状语。

examples.sentence: Comparing to my old bike, this new one is much faster.
examples.trans: 和我的旧自行车相比，这辆新的快多了。

examples.sentence: Comparing to the small town where I grew up, this city has many more restaurants and shops.
examples.trans: 与我长大的小镇相比，这座城市有更多的餐馆和商店。

examples.sentence: Comparing to the brochure, the town had more bins.
examples.trans: 和手册比，镇子垃圾桶更多。

examples.sentence: Comparing to a crowded tour, the slow path was luxury.
examples.trans: 和拥挤的团游比，慢路是奢侈。

examples.sentence: She kept comparing to home and then stopped, which helped.
examples.trans: 她不停拿家乡比，后来停了，这有帮助。

examples.sentence: Comparing to a visa-free neighbour is not a fair test of a poorer station.
examples.trans: 拿免签邻居来比，不是对更穷车站的公平测试。

based on.usageZh: 介词短语，后接名词、代词或名词性短语。常用作状语或后置定语，表示“以……为基础/依据”。口语和书面语都常见，但正式写作中更常用。

examples.sentence: The story is based on a real train.
examples.trans: 这故事基于一列真火车。

examples.sentence: Advice based on brochures will miss the closed tap.
examples.trans: 基于手册的建议会错过关掉的水龙头。

examples.sentence: Their route was based on where relatives still kept keys.
examples.trans: 他们的路线基于亲戚仍留着钥匙的地方。

examples.sentence: Based on the weather forecast, the sports meeting has been put off until next Friday.
examples.trans: 根据天气预报，运动会被推迟到了下周五。

examples.sentence: The report, based on data collected from over 2,000 teenagers, reveals a clear link between sleep and memory.
examples.trans: 这份基于2000多名青少年数据收集的报告揭示了睡眠与记忆之间的明确联系。

examples.sentence: Policy based on photographs will underfund the sweepers.
examples.trans: 基于照片的政策会少资助扫地的人。

crowds of.usageZh: 名词短语，后接复数名词，尤指“people”。表示“成群的、大量的（人）”。多用于描述公共场所、节假日或热门景点的拥挤场景。

examples.sentence: Crowds of children ran to the playground after lunch.
examples.trans: 午饭后，成群的孩子们跑向操场。

examples.sentence: Crowds of fans waited outside the stadium to see the basketball star.
examples.trans: 成群的球迷在体育馆外等候，想见那位篮球明星。

examples.sentence: Crowds of cameras arrived before the cleaners left.
examples.trans: 成群相机在清洁工离开前到达。

examples.sentence: Crowds of passengers gathered around the information desk after the flight was suddenly cancelled.
examples.trans: 航班突然取消后，成群的乘客围在咨询台周围。

examples.sentence: Crowds of cheap tickets can still mean one crowded toilet.
examples.trans: 成堆便宜票仍可能意味着一个拥挤厕所。

examples.sentence: Managing crowds of visitors without crowds of bins is a dare.
examples.trans: 管理成群游客却没有成群垃圾桶，是一种挑衅。

trade it for.usageZh: 动词短语，结构为 trade + 宾语 + for + 交换物，表示“用……交换……”。常与 would not / wouldn't 连用，表示“不愿舍弃某物去换取另一物”，带有情感色彩。

examples.sentence: I have a red pencil, and my friend wants to trade it for a blue one.
examples.trans: 我有一支红铅笔，我的朋友想用一支蓝铅笔来换。

examples.sentence: My little brother offered me his toy car, but I wouldn't trade my football for it.
examples.trans: 弟弟把他的玩具车给我，但我不愿意用我的足球去换。

examples.sentence: They traded the palace ticket for an afternoon of shade.
examples.trans: 他们用宫殿票换了一个下午的树荫。

examples.sentence: He would not trade it for a faster seat without a window.
examples.trans: 没有窗的更快座位，他不愿拿来换。

examples.sentence: Trade speed for talk and the journey lengthens in the good way.
examples.trans: 用速度换谈话，旅程会以好的方式变长。

examples.sentence: Cities trade quiet for numbers, then buy noise machines.
examples.trans: 城市用安静换数字，然后去买噪声机器。

used to be.usageZh: 短语，后接名词、形容词或动词原形，表示过去的状态或习惯，现在已不再如此。常用于对比过去和现在。口语和书面语都常见，否定形式为 didn't use to be 或 used not to be。

examples.sentence: My dad used to be a cook, but now he works in an office.
examples.trans: 我爸爸以前是个厨师，但现在他在办公室工作。

examples.sentence: This street used to be very quiet, but now it is full of cars every morning.
examples.trans: 这条街过去很安静，但现在每天早上都挤满了车。

examples.sentence: She used to be afraid of speaking in public, but she became confident after joining the debate club.
examples.trans: 她过去害怕当众讲话，但加入辩论社后变得自信了。

examples.sentence: The building that now houses the city library used to be a railway station until the late 1990s.
examples.trans: 现在用作市图书馆的那栋楼，在20世纪90年代末之前曾是一个火车站。

examples.sentence: What used to be a path is now a photographed line.
examples.trans: 曾经是小路的东西，现在是一条被拍照的线。

examples.sentence: A town that used to be for workers now rents their windows to tourists.
examples.trans: 一座曾经属于工人的镇子，现在把他们的窗户租给游客。

first of all.usageZh: 副词短语，用于引出第一个要点、理由或步骤，常与 then, second, finally 等连用。通常放在句首，后面用逗号隔开。口语和书面语都常用，语气比 firstly 更自然。

examples.sentence: First of all, wash your hands before you eat anything.
examples.trans: 首先，吃东西之前要洗手。

examples.sentence: First of all, we need to find out why the computer keeps turning itself off.
examples.trans: 首先，我们需要弄清楚电脑为什么总是自动关机。

examples.sentence: First of all, check whether the night train still exists.
examples.trans: 首先，确认夜车是否还在。

examples.sentence: First of all, the report points out that regular exercise can significantly reduce the risk of heart disease.
examples.trans: 首先，报告指出，经常锻炼可以显著降低患心脏病的风险。

examples.sentence: First of all, the child needed a toilet, not a palace.
examples.trans: 首先，孩子需要厕所，不是宫殿。

examples.sentence: First of all, a journey is a bladder and a bench; then it is a view.
examples.trans: 首先，旅程是膀胱和长凳；然后才是景色。

compared to.usageZh: 介词短语，用于引出比较对象，意为“与……相比”。可放在句首或句末。compared to 和 compared with 在多数情况下可互换，但 compared to 更常用于强调相似性，compared with 更常用于强调差异。

examples.sentence: Compared to the plane, the train was calm.
examples.trans: 和飞机比，火车很平静。

examples.sentence: The weather in Kunming is warm all year compared to many other cities in China.
examples.trans: 与中国许多其他城市相比，昆明的天气全年都很温暖。

examples.sentence: Compared to a brochure, the tap was more important.
examples.trans: 和手册比，水龙头更重要。

examples.sentence: Cheap stays, compared to palaces, still need clean sheets.
examples.trans: 便宜住处和宫殿相比，仍需要干净床单。

examples.sentence: Compared to the photographed square, the laundry was friendlier.
examples.trans: 和被拍照的广场比，洗衣店更友善。

examples.sentence: Compared to a visa, a missed train is a small grief.
examples.trans: 和签证相比，误一班火车是小悲伤。

from door to door.usageZh: 副词短语，常用来描述运输或服务的直达性，表示“从出发地直接到目的地”。可修饰动词如 deliver、travel、take、send 等。口语和书面语都常见，尤其用于物流、交通场景。

examples.sentence: The school bus takes us from door to door every day.
examples.trans: 校车每天把我们门到门地接送。

examples.sentence: They travelled from door to door with one backpack.
examples.trans: 他们用一个背包门到门地旅行。

examples.sentence: A taxi from door to door cost more than the train.
examples.trans: 门到门的出租车比火车贵。

examples.sentence: From door to door, the journey was eight hours of kind strangers.
examples.trans: 从门到门，旅程是八小时善良的陌生人。

examples.sentence: Services from door to door still leave someone standing in weather.
examples.trans: 门到门的服务，仍让某个人站在天气里。

examples.sentence: Tourism from door to door can skip the street that actually lives.
examples.trans: 门到门的旅游可能跳过真正生活着的那条街。

worth mentioning.usageZh: 形容词短语，表示“值得一提”。常用结构：It is worth mentioning that + 从句；或 Something is worth mentioning。多用于书面语和正式口语中，用来引出补充说明或强调某个亮点。

examples.sentence: My little brother can count to one hundred, and that is worth mentioning.
examples.trans: 我弟弟能数到一百，这件事值得一提。

examples.sentence: It is worth mentioning that our class collected over 200 books for the school library.
examples.trans: 值得一提的是，我们班为学校图书馆收集了200多本书。

examples.sentence: A working tap is worth mentioning more than a golden statue.
examples.trans: 能用的水龙头比金色雕像更值得一提。

examples.sentence: The quieter carriage was worth mentioning to the next traveller.
examples.trans: 更安静的车厢值得告诉下一位旅客。

examples.sentence: What is particularly worth mentioning is that the author wrote the entire novel while working a full-time job.
examples.trans: 特别值得一提的是，作者是在做全职工作的同时写完了整部小说。

examples.sentence: A destination worth mentioning should mention its night shift too.
examples.trans: 值得一提的目的地，也应提及它的夜班。

take part in.usageZh: 动词短语，后接名词或动名词，表示“参加、参与”。比 join 更强调参与活动或事件的过程。可用于体育、比赛、社会活动、讨论等多种场景，口语和书面语都常用。

examples.sentence: I want to take part in the school sports meeting this year.
examples.trans: 我今年想参加学校运动会。

examples.sentence: Many students in our grade will take part in the English speech contest next Friday.
examples.trans: 我们年级的许多学生将在下周五参加英语演讲比赛。

examples.sentence: To take part in a festival you may need a neighbour's invitation.
examples.trans: 要参加节庆，你可能需要邻居的邀请。

examples.sentence: She did not take part in the crowded tour.
examples.trans: 她没有参加拥挤的团游。

examples.sentence: She was reluctant to take part in the debate at first, but once she started speaking, her arguments proved remarkably persuasive.
examples.trans: 她起初不愿参加辩论，但一旦开始发言，她的论点被证明非常有说服力。

examples.sentence: Tourists who take part in a place should also take part in its bins.
examples.trans: 参与一个地方的游客，也应参与它的垃圾桶。

a lot of.usageZh: 形容词短语，修饰可数名词复数或不可数名词，表示数量多。口语和书面语都常用，语气比 many 和 much 更随意。注意：a lot of 不用于正式程度极高的学术写作，但在日常交流和一般写作中非常自然。

examples.sentence: There are a lot of apples on the tree in my grandpa's garden.
examples.trans: 我爷爷的花园里那棵树上有许多苹果。

examples.sentence: My sister drinks a lot of milk every morning because she wants to grow taller.
examples.trans: 我妹妹每天早上喝很多牛奶，因为她想长得更高。

examples.sentence: If you spend a lot of time practicing the piano, you will see real improvement soon.
examples.trans: 如果你花大量时间练习钢琴，你很快就会看到真正的进步。

examples.sentence: Moving to a new city requires a lot of courage, especially when you don't know anyone there.
examples.trans: 搬到一个新城市需要很大的勇气，尤其是当你在那里一个人都不认识的时候。

examples.sentence: The researchers collected a lot of data over the three-year period, yet the results remained inconclusive.
examples.trans: 研究人员在三年期间收集了大量数据，但结果仍然没有定论。

examples.sentence: A lot of evidence suggests that consistent sleep patterns contribute more to academic performance than last-minute cramming does.
examples.trans: 大量证据表明，规律的睡眠模式比考前临时抱佛脚对学业表现的贡献更大。

pros and cons.usageZh: 名词短语，总是以复数形式使用，表示事物的正反两面。常与动词 weigh、consider、discuss、evaluate 搭配。语体偏正式，但在日常讨论中也常用。注意不要拆开写成 pro and con。

examples.sentence: My dad wrote down the pros and cons of buying a new bike before he said yes.
examples.trans: 我爸爸在同意之前把买新自行车的利与弊写了下来。

examples.sentence: Before choosing a summer camp, let's list the pros and cons of each one together.
examples.trans: 在选择夏令营之前，我们一起把每个夏令营的优缺点列出来吧。

examples.sentence: The pros and cons of a window seat include sunburn.
examples.trans: 靠窗座位的利弊包括晒伤。

examples.sentence: The committee spent two hours weighing the pros and cons of relocating the school library to the new building.
examples.trans: 委员会花了两个小时权衡把学校图书馆迁到新楼的利弊。

examples.sentence: She wrote the pros and cons in the same notebook as the tickets.
examples.trans: 她把利弊和车票写在同一个本子里。

examples.sentence: A balanced argument should present the pros and cons of genetic engineering without letting emotional appeals overshadow factual analysis.
examples.trans: 一篇均衡的议论文应当呈现基因工程的利弊，而不让情感诉求盖过事实分析。

break time.usageZh: 名词短语，表示“休息时间”或“假期”。常作宾语或表语，前面可用形容词修饰，如 short break time、common break time。口语和书面语均可使用，学校场景中尤其常见。

examples.sentence: Break time is for water.
examples.trans: 休息时间用来喝水。

examples.sentence: The train's break time was a platform with one tap.
examples.trans: 火车的休息时间是只有一个水龙头的月台。

examples.sentence: The library is always crowded during break time because many students go there to read quietly.
examples.trans: 休息时间图书馆总是很拥挤，因为许多学生去那里安静地看书。

examples.sentence: A holiday without break time is just a farther shift.
examples.trans: 没有休息时间的假期，只是更远的一班。

examples.sentence: Drivers need real break time, not a slogan on the cab wall.
examples.trans: 司机需要真正的休息时间，不是驾驶室墙上的口号。

examples.sentence: Cities that sell 24-hour fun still owe someone a break time.
examples.trans: 贩卖24小时欢乐的城市，仍欠某个人一段休息。

break away from.usageZh: 动词短语，后接名词或名词短语，表示“摆脱、脱离”某种状态、群体、习惯或传统。可用于具体或抽象语境，如 break away from tradition、break away from the group。书面语和口语均常见。

examples.sentence: The little dog tried to break away from the rope.
examples.trans: 小狗试图挣脱绳子。

examples.sentence: He decided to break away from his bad habit of staying up too late.
examples.trans: 他决定改掉熬夜太晚的坏习惯。

examples.sentence: Break away from the pin on the map if the queue is a kilometre.
examples.trans: 如果队伍有一公里，就脱离地图上的图钉。

examples.sentence: To develop your own style as a writer, you need to break away from imitating others and find your own voice.
examples.trans: 要形成自己的写作风格，你需要摆脱模仿他人，找到自己的声音。

examples.sentence: To break away from a photographed route is a kind of manners.
examples.trans: 脱离被拍照的路线，是一种礼貌。

examples.sentence: A town that cannot break away from one famous corner will choke it.
examples.trans: 无法脱离某一个著名角落的镇子，会把它噎死。

turn out to be.usageZh: 动词短语，后接形容词或名词，表示“结果是、证明是”。结构为：主语 + turn out to be + 形容词/名词。常用于描述与预期不同或出乎意料的结果，口语和书面语均适用。

examples.sentence: The shortcut turned out to be longer.
examples.trans: 捷径结果更长。

examples.sentence: The new student seemed shy at first, but she turned out to be very friendly and funny.
examples.trans: 那位新同学起初看起来很害羞，但结果她非常友好又有趣。

examples.sentence: The path looked short on the map, but it turned out to be a long and tiring walk through the hills.
examples.trans: 这条路在地图上看起来很短，但结果却是一段漫长而累人的山路。

examples.sentence: What initially appeared to be a minor technical problem turned out to be a serious security issue affecting thousands of users.
examples.trans: 最初看似一个小技术问题，结果却是一个影响数千用户的严重安全漏洞。

examples.sentence: The unusual route turned out to be the one with water.
examples.trans: 不寻常的路线结果是有水的那条。

examples.sentence: A magnificent square can turn out to be a frying pan at noon.
examples.trans: 壮丽的广场中午可能变成平底锅。

grammar.key: Present Perfect Tense / 现在完成时
grammar.title: 现在完成时：旅行经历、结果与 for/since
grammar.titleEn: Present perfect for travel experience and unfinished time
grammar.usage:
现在完成时由“have/has + 过去分词”构成，核心功能是连接过去与现在。它主要表达两类含义：一是过去发生的动作对现在造成的影响或结果，例如“I have lost my key”强调现在钥匙不见了；二是从过去某一时间开始一直持续到现在的动作或状态，例如“She has lived here since 2015”强调从2015年至今一直住在这里。肯定句用“主语 + have/has + 过去分词”，否定句在 have/has 后加 not，疑问句把 have/has 提到主语前。

在高中阶段，现在完成时不仅要掌握“已完成”和“未完成”两种基本用法，还要重点区分它与一般过去时的语域差异。一般过去时只陈述过去某个具体时间发生的动作，与现在无关，常与 yesterday、last week、in 2010 等明确的过去时间连用；而现在完成时不与这类具体过去时间连用，常与 already、yet、just、ever、never、so far、up to now、for + 时间段、since + 时间点等连用。例如“I saw that movie yesterday”只是说明昨天看了电影，而“I have seen that movie”则强调我现在知道电影内容，或者有相关经验。

初中用法通常只要求识别 for 和 since 引导的持续状态，以及 already、yet 在肯定和否定句中的位置。高中用法则进一步要求掌握 have been to、have gone to、have been in 的区别，理解现在完成进行时与现在完成时的细微差异，并能在书面语中根据语境判断是否需要用现在完成时来体现“过去对现在的影响”。此外，高中还常考查现在完成时在时间状语从句中的特殊用法，例如在“It is the first time that...”句型中，从句要用现在完成时。

易错点方面，第一，不要把现在完成时与表示具体过去时间的状语连用，不能说“I have seen him yesterday”；第二，have gone to 表示“去了某地还没回来”，have been to 表示“去过某地已经回来”，两者不可混淆；第三，since 后面接时间点，for 后面接时间段，不能说“since two years”；第四，在“It is + 时间段 + since...”句型中，since 从句常用一般过去时，主句用现在完成时或一般现在时，需要根据语境判断。

否定句：主语 + have/has + not + 过去分词（+ 其他）

grammar.key: Gerund as Subject / 动名词作主语
grammar.title: 动名词作主语（旅行活动名物化）
grammar.titleEn: Gerund as subject in travel contexts
grammar.usage:
动名词是动词的 -ing 形式，在句中起名词作用。当动名词或动名词短语位于句首充当主语时，表示一种泛指的、习惯性的或抽象的活动或概念，而不是某一次具体的动作。核心结构为“动名词（短语）+ 谓语动词”，此时谓语动词一律用第三人称单数形式。例如：Traveling gives you a chance to learn something new. 否定形式是在动名词前直接加 not，如：Not exercising regularly can lead to health problems. 疑问形式通常借助 it 作形式主语来构成，如：Is it worth spending so much time on this?

在初中阶段，动名词作主语主要考查“句首动词用 -ing 形式”以及“谓语动词用单数”这两个基本点。进入高中后，动名词作主语的使用范围明显扩大：一是与 it 形式主语结构结合，如 It is no use doing sth. / It is worth doing sth. / It is a waste of time doing sth.；二是动名词可以带有自己的逻辑主语，如 Tom's being late again made the teacher angry；三是动名词作主语时常与不定式作主语形成对比，动名词侧重“泛指、已有经验或一般性事实”，不定式侧重“具体、将来或一次性动作”。

动名词作主语与不定式作主语是高中阶段的重要对比点。动名词作主语通常表示抽象的、习惯性的或已知的活动，如 Swimming is good for health. 而不定式作主语往往表示具体的、尚未发生的动作，如 To swim in this river is dangerous. 在 It is + 形容词 + doing/to do 结构中，部分形容词有固定搭配倾向，如 important, necessary, difficult 后多用不定式，而 no use, no good, worth, a waste of time 后只用动名词。

易错点一：句首动词形式判断。祈使句用动词原形开头，动名词作主语用 -ing 形式开头，两者不可混淆。例如：Reading books opens your mind.（动名词作主语）与 Read the book carefully.（祈使句）。易错点二：动名词作主语时，谓语动词的单复数。无论动名词短语有多长、是否带有宾语或状语，谓语动词始终用单数。易错点三：动名词的否定形式。否定词 not 必须放在动名词之前，不能放在谓语动词之后。易错点四：动名词与现在分词作定语或状语的区分。动名词作主语时是名词性功能，而现在分词作状语时表示伴随或原因，如 Hearing the news, she cried.（现在分词作状语，不是主语）。
forms: Gerund (phrase) + 单数谓语动词：Traveling gives you a chance to learn.
Not + Gerund + 单数谓语动词：Not sleeping enough affects your memory.
It + is + no use/no good/worth + Gerund：It is no use crying over spilt milk.
Gerund + 宾语/状语（扩展的动名词短语作主语）：Learning a foreign language takes time.
逻辑主语（名词所有格/形容词性物主代词）+ Gerund + 谓语：Tom's being late again made the teacher angry.
It + is + 形容词（important/necessary/difficult）+ to do（对比：不定式作主语）：It is important to learn English well.
notes: 主语用单数谓语。
介词后用动名词。

不定式更偏具体一次性。

grammar.title: 叠用比较级：越来越挤、越来越慢、越来越少班次
grammar.usage:
比较结构用于说明两个事物之间的异同或相对关系。高中阶段最核心的是 compared to/with 和 comparing to 两种形式。compared to/with 是过去分词短语，在句中作状语，通常放在句首或句尾，表示“与……相比”，其逻辑主语与主句主语一致。例如：Compared with his brother, Tom is more outgoing.（与他哥哥相比，汤姆更外向。）comparing to 是现在分词短语，带有主动意味，常出现在非正式口语或较随意的书面语中，表示“如果把……拿来比较的话”，但高中书面表达中更推荐使用 compared to/with。

肯定句结构为“Compared to/with + 名词/代词, 主句”，否定形式一般在主句中使用否定词，如 Compared to last year, the situation is not better. 疑问形式则通常借助主句的疑问结构，如 Compared with before, has anything changed? 需要注意的是，compared to/with 本身不随人称和时态变化，因为它是一个固定的分词短语。

compare A with B 侧重“把A和B进行对比，找出异同”，常用于具体分析；compare A to B 除了可以表示“把A和B相比”之外，还常表示“把A比作B”，具有比喻色彩。例如：We compared the results with the original data.（我们把结果与原始数据进行了对比。）Shakespeare compared the world to a stage.（莎士比亚把世界比作舞台。）高中阶段还常见 in comparison with/by comparison 等介词短语，用于正式书面语，如 In comparison with other countries, this figure is relatively low.

初中阶段主要要求掌握 compared to/with 的基本含义和简单句中的位置，以及 compare A with B 的固定搭配。高中阶段则进一步要求：能在复杂句中使用分词短语作状语，注意逻辑主语一致；能区分 compare to 与 compare with 的语义侧重；能在书面表达中灵活运用 in comparison with、by comparison、relative to 等更正式的比较表达；能识别 comparing to 的非正式语域特征，并在正式写作中替换为 compared to/with。

易错点一：分词短语的逻辑主语问题。Compared to/with 的逻辑主语必须与主句主语一致，否则会造成悬垂结构。例如：Compared with other students, the exam was easy for him. 这句话是错误的，因为 compared 的逻辑主语应该是“他”，而不是“考试”。应改为：Compared with other students, he found the exam easy.
易错点二：compare to 与 compare with 的混用。在表示“比喻”时只能用 compare A to B，不能用 with。例如：Life is often compared to a journey.（生活常被比作一段旅程。）
易错点三：comparing to 在正式写作中的使用。高中书面表达和高考作文中，应避免使用 comparing to 作状语，统一使用 compared to/with。
易错点四：compared to 与 compared with 在多数情况下可以互换，但 compared to 更常用于口语和一般性比较，compared with 更侧重细致对比，尤其在学术或正式语体中。
forms: Compared to/with + 名词/代词, + 主句（过去分词短语作状语）
主句 + compared to/with + 名词/代词（分词短语后置）
compare A with B（将A与B进行对比，找出异同）
compare A to B（将A比作B；也可表示将A与B相比）
In comparison with + 名词/代词, + 主句（正式书面语）
By comparison, + 主句（相比之下，用于句首过渡）
notes: 不要 more and more louder。
people 用 more and more people。
fewer 接可数。
可与 become/get 连用。
不要和 the more 句型零件混用。

grammar.key: Modal Verb for Suggestion / 表建议的情态动词
grammar.title: should / Let's / Why don't / had better：旅行建议
grammar.usage:
本语法点围绕“提出建议”这一交际功能展开。核心结构是“Why not + 动词原形...?”，它并不是由单个情态动词构成，而是以疑问句形式表达一种委婉、鼓励性的建议，语气比“You should...”更柔和，相当于“How about...?”或“Let's...”。该结构在口语和书面语中都很常见，尤其在邀请对方尝试某事、改变计划或采取行动时使用。

肯定式建议常用“Why not + 动词原形”，如：Why not plan a trip away from the routine we live in every day? 否定式建议则常借助“Why don't you/we + 动词原形...?”来表达，如：Why don't we take a short break? 疑问式本身即为建议，不需要再添加其他疑问词。回答时通常用“Good idea!”“That sounds great!”“Sure, let's do that.”等表示接受。

与近义结构对比：should 表示“应该做”，语气较为直接，带有一定义务感；could 表示“可以/不妨”，语气更委婉，给对方更多选择空间；may/might 用于建议时语气更正式、更弱，常见于书面语或较正式场合，如“You might consider taking a different approach.”。而“Why not...?”和“Why don't you/we...?”则更口语化，带有邀请和鼓励色彩。

初中阶段主要要求掌握“Why not + 动词原形”和“Why don't you/we + 动词原形”的基本用法，并能区分其与询问原因的“Why...?”句型。高中阶段则进一步要求理解情态动词在建议功能中的语气差异，如 should/could/may/might 的委婉程度、正式程度，并能在书面表达中根据语境选择恰当的建议方式。

易错点：1. “Why not”后必须接动词原形，不能接动名词或不定式；2. “Why don't you/we”后同样接动词原形，且注意主语 you/we 不能省略；3. 不要把“Why not...?”与询问原因的“Why...?”混淆，后者需要助动词和主语，如“Why are you late?”；4. 在正式书面语中，过多使用“Why not...?”可能显得口语化，高考书面表达中可适当替换为“It is advisable to...”“You might consider...”等结构。
forms: Why not + 动词原形...?  （为什么不……呢？）
Why don't you/we + 动词原形...?  （你/我们为什么不……呢？）
You should + 动词原形...  （你应该……）
You could + 动词原形...  （你不妨/可以……）
You may/might + 动词原形...  （你可以/或许可以……）
It is advisable to + 动词原形...  （建议做……，书面语）
notes: should 后无 to。
must 更强制，can 表能力不是建议。

Let's + 原形。
should have done 责备过去。

grammar.key: Adverbial Clause of Condition (No matter...) / 条件状语从句 (No matter...)
grammar.title: no matter how/what/who/where 与 however/whatever/wherever
grammar.usage:
“no matter + 疑问词”结构用于引导让步状语从句，表示“无论……都……”，强调主句所述的情况不会因为从句条件的变化而改变。常见疑问词包括 where, what, who, how, when, which 等，例如 no matter where（无论在哪里）、no matter what（无论什么）、no matter how（无论怎样）。该结构在句中作状语，修饰主句的谓语动词或整个主句。

在肯定句中，结构通常为“No matter + 疑问词 + 主语 + 谓语，主句”；否定形式主要体现在主句或从句的否定词上，例如“No matter what he says, I won't believe him.”。疑问形式一般针对主句提问，例如“Will you support me no matter what happens?”。需要注意的是，从句本身不使用疑问句语序，而是使用陈述句语序。

“no matter + 疑问词”与“疑问词 + ever”在让步状语从句中通常可以互换，例如“No matter where you go”相当于“Wherever you go”。但两者存在重要区别：“no matter + 疑问词”只能引导让步状语从句，不能引导名词性从句；而“whatever / whoever / whichever”等既可以引导让步状语从句，也可以引导主语从句、宾语从句等名词性从句。例如可以说“You can take whatever you like”，但不能说“You can take no matter what you like”。

初中阶段主要要求掌握“no matter what / where / how”等常见搭配的基本含义和简单用法，通常与一般现在时连用表示将来意义。高中阶段则进一步要求理解该结构与“疑问词 + ever”的互换条件及限制，能够在书面表达中准确区分让步状语从句与名词性从句，并学会使用“no matter how + 形容词/副词”等较为复杂的结构来表达程度让步。

易错点一：从句语序误用疑问句语序。例如“No matter where is he”是错误的，应改为“No matter where he is”。易错点二：将“no matter + 疑问词”误用于名词性从句。例如“I don't know no matter what he wants”是错误的，应改为“I don't know what he wants”。易错点三：时态误用。在表示将来意义时，从句通常用一般现在时，而不是将来时。易错点四：混淆“no matter how”与“no matter what”的搭配。“no matter how”后接形容词或副词，如“no matter how hard it is”；“no matter what”后接名词或单独使用，如“no matter what happens”。
forms: No matter + 疑问词 + 主语 + 谓语，主句
No matter + where/what/who/how/when/which + 从句，主句
No matter how + 形容词/副词 + 主语 + 谓语，主句
主句 + no matter + 疑问词 + 从句（从句可后置）
疑问词 + ever + 从句 ≈ No matter + 疑问词 + 从句（仅限让步状语从句）
No matter + 疑问词 + 从句，主句（从句用一般现在时表将来）

no matter how 后接形容词/副词再接主谓。
however expensive it is = no matter how expensive it is。
whether 不能丢 or。
让步不等于条件 unless。

grammar.key: Adjective + Infinitive (It's + adj + to do) / 形容词+不定式
grammar.title: It is + adj + to do / for sb to do / of sb to do / that
grammar.titleEn: Introductory it with adjectives and infinitives
grammar.usage:
本语法点的核心结构是“It is + 形容词 + (for/of sb) + to do sth”，其中 it 作形式主语，真正的主语是后面的不定式短语。该结构用于评价一个动作、行为或情况，表达“做某事是……的”。肯定句如：It is important to keep calm. 否定句在 is 后加 not：It is not easy to change a habit. 疑问句将 is/was 提前：Is it necessary to bring an umbrella? 回答时常用 It is / It isn't。

在高中阶段，该结构需要进一步区分 for sb 和 of sb 的用法。当形容词描述事情的性质（如 important, difficult, necessary, possible, challenging）时，用 for sb；当形容词描述人的品格或特征（如 kind, nice, careless, wise, brave）时，用 of sb。例如：It was wise of her to refuse the offer. 这类句子常可改写为 She was wise to refuse the offer. 而 for sb 结构一般不能这样改写。

该结构还与 too…to… 和 enough to… 形成拓展关系。too + adj + to do 表示“太……而不能做”，本身含有否定意义；adj + enough + to do 表示“足够……可以做”。例如：It is too late to apologize. / It is early enough to catch the train. 高中书面语中常将 too…to 与 so…that… 句型互换，但要注意 too…to 本身已含否定，不能再加 not。

初中阶段主要要求掌握 It is + adj + to do 的基本评价功能，以及少量 for sb 的用法；高中阶段则要求系统掌握 for/of 的语义差异、too…to 与 enough to 的转换、不定式与动名词在类似语境中的区别，以及该结构在书面表达中的高级替换。

易错点一：形容词后误用动名词。不能说 It is important doing exercise. 应说 It is important to do exercise. 易错点二：主谓一致错误。动词始终与形式主语 It 一致，用 is/was，不受后面名词影响。易错点三：混淆 for 和 of。判断方法是看形容词能否修饰人：能修饰人用 of，不能则用 for。易错点四：too…to 结构中重复否定。例如 It is too difficult to not understand 是错误的，应直接说 It is too difficult to understand. 易错点五：在书面表达中过度使用 It is adj to do 开头，导致句式单一，高中写作应适当替换为 Doing sth is adj 或名词短语作主语。

grammar.key: Present Simple Passive Voice / 一般现在时被动语态
grammar.title: 一般现在时被动 am/is/are + 过去分词，兼情态被动与 It is said that
grammar.titleEn: Present simple passive and modal passives
grammar.usage:
一般现在时被动语态的核心结构是：主语 + am/is/are + 过去分词（V-ed/V3）。它用于强调动作的承受者，或者当动作的执行者不明确、不重要、不言自明时。肯定句如：The bridge is repaired every year. 否定句在 be 动词后加 not：The bridge is not repaired every year. 一般疑问句把 be 动词提到句首：Is the bridge repaired every year? 特殊疑问句则用“疑问词 + be + 主语 + 过去分词”：When is the bridge repaired?

与主动语态相比，被动语态把焦点从“谁做”转移到“什么事被做”。主动句 They clean the room every day. 强调 they 的行为；被动句 The room is cleaned every day. 强调 room 的状态或常规安排。当需要说明执行者时，用 by + 执行者：The room is cleaned by the staff every day. 但高中阶段要特别注意：并非所有主动句都适合改成被动句，不及物动词（如 happen, appear, arrive）没有被动语态。

初中阶段一般只要求掌握 am/is/are + 过去分词的基本构成，以及“被……”的中文翻译。高中阶段则要进一步理解：被动语态在说明文、新闻报道、科普文章、操作流程和正式书面语中的高频使用；by 短语的省略条件；以及“get + 过去分词”在口语中表被动的非正式用法（如 The window got broken）。此外，高中还需辨析被动语态与系表结构的区别：The door is closed. 既可理解为“门被关上了”（被动动作），也可理解为“门是关着的”（状态），需根据语境判断。

易错点一：be 动词与主语的人称和数不一致。例如主语是复数时误用 is：The rooms is cleaned. 应为 The rooms are cleaned. 易错点二：不规则动词的过去分词形式记错。例如 take 的过去分词是 taken，不是 took；write 是 written，不是 wrote。易错点三：把不及物动词用于被动语态。例如 The accident was happened. 是错误的，应为 The accident happened. 易错点四：在不需要说明执行者时硬加 by 短语，导致句子累赘。例如 English is spoken by people all over the world. 中的 by people 通常可以省略。
forms: 肯定式：主语 + am/is/are + 过去分词（+ by + 执行者）
否定式：主语 + am/is/are + not + 过去分词
一般疑问式：Am/Is/Are + 主语 + 过去分词？
特殊疑问式：疑问词 + am/is/are + 主语 + 过去分词？
口语非正式被动：主语 + get(s) + 过去分词
含情态动词的被动（拓展）：主语 + 情态动词 + be + 过去分词

复数用 are。

形容词比较级用于对两个人、事物、概念或状态进行程度上的对比，核心结构为“比较级 + than + 比较对象”。在初中阶段，学生主要掌握单音节和部分双音节形容词加-er（如 tall → taller, big → bigger, heavy → heavier）以及多音节形容词前加 more（如 beautiful → more beautiful），并用 than 引出被比较对象。进入高中阶段后，比较级的用法进一步拓展：一是比较级前可使用程度副词或短语进行修饰，如 much, far, a lot, even, still, a bit, a little, slightly, rather, no, any 等，以表达差异的大小或强调；二是比较级可出现在更复杂的句法结构中，如“the + 比较级, the + 比较级”（越……越……）、“比较级 + and + 比较级”（越来越……）、“the + 比较级 + of the two”（两者中较……的一个）；三是在书面语和正式语域中，比较级常与替代词 that/those 连用，避免重复名词，如 The climate here is milder than that of Beijing。

肯定句结构为“A + be/动词 + 比较级 + than + B”，否定句在 be/助动词后加 not，如“This train is not cheaper than that one.”。疑问句将 be/助动词提前，如“Is this train cheaper than that one?”。需要注意的是，比较级本身不直接构成否定，否定的是整个谓语部分。

与近义结构对比：比较级（comparative）用于两者之间的比较，而最高级（superlative）用于三者或三者以上的比较。此外，“as + 形容词原级 + as”表示“和……一样”，其否定形式“not as/so + 原级 + as”表示“不如……”，这与比较级在语义上有重叠，但语体不同——比较级更直接，as...as 结构更强调等同或差异的程度。高中阶段还需区分“more + 形容词”构成的比较级与“more + 名词”表示数量更多的用法，例如 more comfortable（更舒适的）与 more money（更多的钱）。

易错点方面：第一，不可同时使用 -er 和 more，如 more cheaper 是典型错误；第二，不规则形容词的比较级需单独记忆，如 good → better, bad → worse, far → farther/further, little → less, many/much → more；第三，以辅音字母加 y 结尾的形容词变比较级时，y 要变为 i 再加 -er（如 happy → happier），而以元音字母加 y 结尾的则直接加 -er（如 grey → greyer）；第四，重读闭音节且末尾只有一个辅音字母的形容词，需双写该辅音字母再加 -er（如 hot → hotter, thin → thinner, big → bigger）。
forms: 单音节/部分双音节形容词：adj. + -er + than + 比较对象（tall → taller than）
多音节/部分双音节形容词：more + adj. + than + 比较对象（more expensive than）
否定结构：A + be/助动词 + not + 比较级 + than + B（is not cheaper than）
疑问结构：Be/助动词 + A + 比较级 + than + B?（Is this train cheaper than that one?）
程度修饰：much / far / a lot / even / still / a bit / a little / slightly / rather + 比较级（much cheaper than）
特殊句型：the + 比较级, the + 比较级（The sooner, the better.）；比较级 + and + 比较级（better and better）
notes: 肯定用 as...as，不用 so...as（否定可用 so）。
后一个 as 不可丢。
many 接可数，much 接不可数。
不要 as more tall as。
twice as expensive as，不是 twice more expensive as（后者也有人说，考场慎用）。

grammar.key: Modal Verb 'can' for Ability/Possibility / 情态动词'can'表能力/可能性
grammar.title: can / could / be able to：能力、可能、许可与 can't have done
grammar.titleEn: Can for ability, possibility, permission, and related forms
grammar.usage:
情态动词 can 的核心结构为“can + 动词原形”，无人称和数的变化，后面不能接 to，也不能接动词的 -ing、-ed 等形式。肯定句用“主语 + can + 动词原形”，否定句用“主语 + cannot/can't + 动词原形”，疑问句把 can 提到主语之前，即“Can + 主语 + 动词原形？”。can 主要表达三类意义：能力、可能性、许可。本讲重点聚焦能力与可能性，并拓展到 could、be able to、may、might 等相关结构。

在初中阶段，can 多用于表达“会做某事”的能力，如 I can swim. 以及“可以”的许可，如 Can I go out? 高中阶段则更强调 can 在语境中的细微差别：can 表“理论上的可能性”时，常指一般情况或事物本身具备的性质，如 It can get very cold in winter. 而 may/might 表“具体事件的可能性”时，语气更弱、更不确定，如 He may come later. 此外，高中还要求掌握 could 作为 can 的过去式，以及 could 用于现在或将来表示更委婉、更不确定的语气。

can 与 be able to 的对比是高中重点。can 只有现在式和过去式 could，没有完成式、进行式或不定式形式，因此当需要表达“将来能够”“已经能够”“想要能够”等意义时，要用 be able to 的相应形式，如 will be able to、have been able to、want to be able to。在表达“过去某次具体做成某事”时，常用 was/were able to 或 managed to，而不用 could，因为 could 多表示过去的一般能力或可能性，不强调“成功做成”。

易错点一：can 后面误加 to，如 I can to swim 是错误的。易错点二：第三人称单数误加 -s，如 He cans swim 是错误的。易错点三：把 can 用于将来能力，如 I will can swim 是错误的，应改为 I will be able to swim。易错点四：在否定句中 can't 可表达强烈的否定推测，意为“不可能”，如 He can't be at home now. 此时语气比 may not/might not 更强。
forms: 肯定式：主语 + can + 动词原形
否定式：主语 + cannot / can't + 动词原形
疑问式：Can + 主语 + 动词原形？
过去式：主语 + could + 动词原形
将来能力：主语 + will be able to + 动词原形
委婉/不确定可能性：主语 + may / might / could + 动词原形
notes: can 后无 to、无 -s。
将来能力 will be able to，不是 will can。
许可：Can I...? May I...? 更正式。
can't 表不可能（推测）。
过去某次成功用 was able to/managed to。

grammar.key: Gerund as Subject / 动名词作主语
grammar.title: 动名词主语再探：It's no use / look forward to / 复合结构
grammar.titleEn: Gerund versus infinitive as subject and after prepositions
grammar.usage:
动名词是动词的 -ing 形式，在句中起名词作用。当动名词或动名词短语作主语时，表示一种泛指的活动、习惯、事实或抽象概念，而不是某一次具体动作。核心结构为“动名词短语 + 单数谓语动词”，因为动名词作主语时整体被视为单数概念。例如：Reading before bed helps me relax.（睡前阅读帮助我放松。）

肯定句直接以动名词短语开头，后接单数谓语；否定形式在动名词前加 not，例如：Not getting enough sleep affects your health.（睡眠不足会影响健康。）疑问形式通常借助形式主语 it 或使用一般疑问句结构，如：Does swimming help you stay fit?（游泳有助于保持健康吗？）在书面语中，也常见“It is + 形容词/名词 + 动名词短语”的结构，如：It is no use crying over spilled milk.（覆水难收。）

动名词作主语与不定式作主语有重要区别。动名词多表示普遍、习惯性、已知或正在进行的活动；不定式多表示具体的、将来的或一次性的动作。例如：Swimming is my favorite sport.（泛指游泳这项运动）与 To swim in that cold river is dangerous.（特指在那条冷河里游泳这件事）。高中阶段需要进一步掌握：某些形容词或名词后习惯用动名词作真正主语，如 no use, no good, worth, fun, a waste of time 等；同时要能识别动名词作主语与现在分词作表语或定语的区别。

初中阶段主要要求掌握动名词作主语的常见表达，如“Playing basketball is fun.”，并记住谓语用单数。高中阶段则要求：1）能区分动名词与不定式作主语的语用差异；2）掌握形式主语 it 的句型转换；3）在书面表达中恰当使用动名词短语作主语来提升句式多样性；4）理解动名词的复合结构作主语，如：His coming late made the teacher angry.（他迟到让老师生气。）

易错点一：动名词作主语时，谓语动词必须用单数，即使动名词短语中包含复数名词。例如：Reading books is important.（读书很重要。）不能说 Reading books are important. 易错点二：不要把进行时态中的现在分词误认为动名词作主语。例如：He is swimming in the pool.（他正在游泳池里游泳。）这里的 swimming 是现在分词，与 is 构成进行时，不是主语。易错点三：动名词的否定形式是 not 放在动名词前面，而不是后面。例如：Not telling the truth is wrong.（不说真话是错误的。）易错点四：在“It is no use/no good + 动名词”结构中，不要用不定式替代动名词。例如：It is no use complaining.（抱怨没有用。）不宜说 It is no use to complain.
forms: 动名词短语 + 单数谓语动词：Swimming is good exercise.
否定形式：Not + 动名词短语 + 单数谓语动词：Not exercising regularly leads to health problems.
疑问形式：Does + 动名词短语 + 谓语动词原形...?：Does reading in dim light hurt your eyes?
形式主语结构：It is + 形容词/名词 + 动名词短语：It is no use arguing with him.
动名词复合结构作主语：名词所有格/形容词性物主代词 + 动名词短语 + 单数谓语：His arriving late surprised everyone.
动名词作主语与不定式作主语对比：Swimming is fun.（泛指） vs To swim in this river is dangerous.（特指）
notes: 主语用单数谓语。
介词后用动名词。
It's no use + gerund。
look forward to + gerund。
不定式更偏具体一次性。
